> Skip, not reject
What is this phrasing? Why do we have something like this on a card?
node src/cli.ts show al-profile; grep -n '"id":"al-profile"' .werk/log.jsonl | head -20 | cut -c1-400

card al-profile  [decided]
A growing decision profile
why: Skipped on purpose. Decisions have not repeated enough yet to earn a standing-preference mechanism. Reopen this if that changes.

The idea still holds: capture how you decide, not what to build, so alignment does not reset every work item. But nothing built so far has hit the same trade-off twice — #werk-stack's six criteria, the tab placement calls, the permission-mode choice were each one-off. Building a profile mechanism now would be process for a problem that has not shown up yet.

Skip, not reject: the difference from #decisionmd (still supported_by, still worth reading if this reopens) is that this is not a dead end, it is deferred until the trigger condition actually occurs — the same class of trade-off coming up a second time.

"Skip, not reject" marks a deferral. The card has its own decided status, but at the time the log had no way to say "deferred". The sentence in the card body fills that gap by hand.

**Where the sentence comes from:**
1. The card was decided on 2026-09-17 in a session that chose not to build a decision profile yet.
2. `decided` alone reads as "we are done with this". That session wanted to say something else: the idea is still good, and it waits for a trigger.
3. The log had no field for that. So the agent wrote the difference into the body. It compares the card to `#decisionmd`, a source the card cites, and it says this is "not a dead end, it is deferred".

**Why it no longer belongs on the card:** the map now has two structured places for this.
- A kill criterion on the card records when to revisit the decision. Here the trigger is "the same class of trade-off comes up a second time". The card has no kill criterion yet.
- `werk reopen --reason postponed` marks a card as paused, not wrong (`#reopen-reason-gap`).

The sentence also breaks `#werk-wording`. "Skip, not reject" and "nothing built so far" describe the session that wrote the card.

**My recommendation:**
1. Keep the card decided. The decision is "no profile mechanism until a trade-off repeats".
2. Add the trigger as a kill criterion with `--form manual`.
3. Remove the "Skip, not reject" paragraph, and keep `#decisionmd` as a supported_by source.

Next: say "fix it" and I add the kill criterion and propose the body change.

I made two changes to `#al-profile`:
1. **Kill criterion, already on the card:** a manual test that fires when the same class of trade-off comes up a second time. The map shows this in the card's kill section.
2. **Rewrite, pending your ✓:**
   - The why line says: "No standing-preference mechanism until the same class of trade-off comes up twice. A one-off decision does not earn one."
   - The "Skip, not reject" paragraph is gone. The trigger now lives in the kill criterion, and the body points to it.
   - `#decisionmd` stays as the starting point for when the trigger fires.

Next: accept the blue rewrite on `#al-profile`.
